target_customer: Developers who want to call many third-party SaaS APIs through one GraphQL endpoint with managed authentication
problem: Most services lacked a GraphQL API, and each needed its own auth and integration work. OneGraph wrapped APIs such as GitHub, Stripe and Salesforce in one GraphQL interface.
product_category: GraphQL API gateway and API authentication

founders.name: Sean Grove
founders.background_notes: Became Principal Architect at Netlify after the acquisition and later built Linzumi. Pre-2018 employers not captured.

founders.name: Daniel Woelfel
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no background. Netlify said he would lead API ecosystem strategy with Grove.

technical_complexity.rationale: Wrapping many REST APIs, often from OpenAPI files, into consistent GraphQL with managed OAuth across many services needs substantial tooling for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: A catalog of maintained integrations and stored auth flows takes sustained effort to rebuild, but the service depended on third-party API terms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Netlify acquired OneGraph on 2021-11-17 and launched API Authentication via Netlify Labs as the first product step.

market_need_then: GraphQL was gaining developer attention in 2018 while most SaaS APIs remained REST, so a unified layer addressed real integration work. No spend data found.

branding.domain_note: Held onegraph.com. A trademark for ONEGRAPH was filed in November 2020 and registered in September 2021 per a trademark database, owner listed in California.
branding.community_and_virality: Founder appeared on podcasts such as Software Engineering Daily and JAMstack Radio, and a developer blog covered it.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in GraphQL developer circles through podcasts and blog posts, but no mascot or community assets found. The name states the idea.

outcome_analysis: OneGraph was a two person team that built a GraphQL layer over third-party APIs and was funded through YC and a small seed round. Netlify acquired it on 2021-11-17 alongside Netlify's 105 million dollar raise, bringing both founders in to lead API ecosystem strategy. The price was not disclosed, so whether this was a strong exit or a soft landing is unclear.
notes: onegraph.com did not resolve during fetch (DNS failure), treated as dead. Seed: Dealroom says about 150K with Y Combinator, SignalFire, Dig Ventures and Pioneer Fund, and BounceWatch dates it September 2018. Both are aggregators, so no round is recorded. No competitor source dated near August 2018 was found. Netlify's acquisition post names OneGraph as backed by YC and SignalFire. Name origin not found.
